title: Getting Started with NanoQuRe
text: NanoQuRe provides quality control tools Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing data. Starting sequencing summary file produced ONT basecaller (Guppy Dorado), package generates interactive plots summary tables, can bundle self-contained HTML report single function call.

title: Getting Started with NanoQuRe
text: NanoQuRe works per-read columns sequencing summary. following columns required complete report: generate_report() accepts either path tab-separated summary file data frame. file, columns listed read. file sample_id column, file name (without directory extension) used sample identifier, passes_filtering may stored logical value, TRUE/FALSE text, 1/0. individual plotting table functions take data frame. case sample_id added user passes_filtering logical: examples use dataset bundled package (1000 reads single MinION run):
code: seq_summary <- vroom::vroom("sequencing_summary.txt", delim = "\t",                             show_col_types = FALSE)  # raw summaries carry no sample identifier seq_summary$sample_id <- "my_sample"  # the pass/fail flag may be read as text; the functions expect a logical column seq_summary$passes_filtering <- as.logical(seq_summary$passes_filtering) library(NanoQuRe)  data(sample_data)

title: Getting Started with NanoQuRe
text: main entry point generate_report(). counts unique sample_id values input, selects single-sample multi-sample template accordingly, renders self-contained HTML file. report written output_dir (working directory default) path returned. output_file file name ; directory given output_dir. platform argument ("minion", default, "promethion") selects flow cell layout pore activity heatmap. Flongle flow cells supported.
code: generate_report(sample_data, output_file = "my_QC_report.html") # a raw summary file from a PromethION run; the sample is named after the file generate_report("sequencing_summary_run42.txt",                 output_file = "run42_QC_report.html",                 output_dir = "reports",                 platform = "promethion")

text: Two datasets used. bundled sample_data object holds 1000 reads single MinION run serves read length Q-score distributions. reads come first minutes last half hour run , illustrate plots follow run time. time-resolved plots therefore use simulated run, generated : 200,000 reads 512 channels 48 h, channels stop producing reads different times translocation speed Q-score decline slowly. data artificial. illustrate plots look like complete run carry biological meaning. Every function returns ordinary plotly object (plot_double() returns named list two), can modified plotly functions embedded R Markdown document. summary tables generate_report() described Getting Started Using Individual Functions vignettes.
code: library(NanoQuRe)  data(sample_data) set.seed(123) # reproducible simulation  n_reads <- 200000 n_channels <- 512 run_seconds <- 48 * 3600  # each channel stops producing reads at its own time channel_end <- pmin(stats::rweibull(n_channels, shape = 1.5, scale = 30) * 3600,                     run_seconds) # channels that live longer contribute more reads channel <- sample(seq_len(n_channels), n_reads, replace = TRUE, prob = channel_end) start_time <- stats::runif(n_reads, min = 0, max = channel_end[channel]) run_fraction <- start_time / run_seconds  # log-normal read lengths; speed and quality decline over the run read_length <- round(stats::rlnorm(n_reads, meanlog = 6.8, sdlog = .9)) + 20 speed <- stats::rnorm(n_reads, mean = 400 - 60 * run_fraction, sd = 25) qscore <- stats::rnorm(n_reads, mean = 12.5 - 2 * run_fraction, sd = 2)  simulated_run <- data.frame(   sample_id = "simulated_run",   run_id = "simulated_run_1",   channel = channel,   start_time = start_time,   duration = read_length / pmax(speed, 50),   sequence_length_template = read_length,   mean_qscore_template = qscore,   # pass/fail threshold of the simulated basecaller   passes_filtering = qscore >= 9 )

text: NanoQuRe reads sequencing summary files produced ONT basecallers (Guppy Dorado) generates interactive plots, summary tables, self-contained HTML QC report, single function call. Unlike packages built around external basecallers/ML toolchains, NanoQuRe pure R package compiled code external system dependencies.

title: NanoQuRe: Quality Control for Oxford Nanopore Sequencing
text: NanoQuRe expects data frame eight columns: run_id, channel, start_time, duration, sequence_length_template, mean_qscore_template, passes_filtering (present Guppy Dorado sequencing summaries), plus sample_id. Raw basecaller summaries contain sample_id: data frame needs added user (one value per sample), whereas file without column generate_report() uses file name (without directory extension) sample identifier. generate_report() accepts data either -memory data frame path tab-separated summary file, eight columns read; passes_filtering may logical, TRUE/FALSE text, 1/0 passed generate_report().

title: NanoQuRe: Quality Control for Oxford Nanopore Sequencing
text: pore_activity_heatmap() (generate_report(), calls ) takes platform argument: "minion" (512 channels, default) "promethion" (3000 channels). Channel numbers outside selected layout stop heatmap, whereas MinION data drawn "promethion" placed wrong layout without error. Multi-sample reports render sample’s pore heatmap independently; single problematic sample (e.g. spanning one run_id) reported inline rather failing whole report. single-sample report likewise shows inline notice instead failing heatmap drawn. MinION PromethION layouts supported; Flongle flow cells (126 channels) . generate_report() warns one sample_id spans several run_id values.

text: Provides quality control tools Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing data. Reads sequencing summary files produced Guppy Dorado generates interactive plots summary tables covering read-length distributions, base quality scores, cumulative yield, sequencing throughput, translocation speed, pore channel activity. single call generate_report() renders self-contained HTML report one summary files, automatic single-sample multi-sample layout selection.
